why_v6: v5 froze the arm at 11.189 s on 238 with the four B0 knobs promoted to code defaults. v6 adds four more measured wins, and the notable thing about all four is that they are B0: the trajectory digest 1f36e75dc00ed2b4 and the outer count 4377 do not move anywhere between b903225 and d68de15. OUTER_GRAPH captures the outer WHILE loop into a CUDA graph and was expected to be N1 (floating-point reassociation); 238 measured h5diff 0 over the full dataset and a literal-zero Gate A at every statepoint, so it is B0 in practice on this deck. MICX_RESIDENT keeps the micro-XS block resident on the device and collapses micx D2H from 18.69 GB to 3.31 GB, which is also the single largest batch win of the whole campaign (+19.3 pct). WP15.1 turns CRAM's mic upload into a device-to-device copy (cram_micx_h2d_mb 0.0). CMFD_BLOCK=64 is a pure launch-shape knob that turns the same work into more, better-occupying blocks (vector_blocks 67 -> 265, the first arm to clear 2x the SM count) and is worth -4.1 pct on a single deck while being flat in batch. Together: 9.808 s against MASTER's 27.2 s, 2.77x.
baseline_commit_note: d68de15 (perf(WP17)) is the tree the 9.808 s number was measured on. The v6 stack itself was measured at 6bdfdc2 (10.206 s) and re-measured at cd3630c after WP15.1 (10.217 s); d68de15 adds only the CMFD_BLOCK knob, which is off by default. The branch tip at the time of writing is bd7a0d3 (perf(WP18)), which adds the rolling-refill scheduler substrate that was measured and NOT adopted - see rejected_and_closed.

benchmark_input.env_note: SELF-DESCRIBING ON PURPOSE, exactly as v5's is. The last five knobs are the phase-2 additions. The four before them (CMFD_FUSE, XE_TXN, RESULT_ASYNC, FLATXS_CTA) are already code DEFAULTS since v5 and an env that omitted them would resolve identically - they stay written out because src/CaseKey.h digests the RAW exported string, so unset and "1" are different case_keys for the same arm.
benchmark_input.env_note_single_vs_batch: THIS ENV IS THE SINGLE-DECK ARM. Two of its knobs must be REMOVED for batch: RASBERY_GPU_CMFD_BLOCK=64 (batch 1176.1 c/h, -0.3 pct, flat) and RASBERY_GPU_OUTER_SEGMENT_V2=1 (batch 1167.8 vs 1179.1 c/h, -1.0 pct). RASBERY_CUDA_SYNC_MODE=blocking is the mirror image: a batch OPTION only, and 8.7 pct SLOWER on a single deck. This is the first arm in the campaign whose single-deck and batch envs genuinely differ, and that divergence is measured, not assumed.

cmfd_block.gate_class: B0 across the WHOLE sweep - this is a launch-shape knob and touches no physics.
cmfd_block.claim: the CMFD/BiCG kernels launch with 64-thread blocks instead of 256, turning the same total work into more, smaller, better-occupying blocks.
cmfd_block.evidence_238: block 29a at d68de15, interleaved warm-up 1 + hot 3, five arms: 256 -> 10.228 s, 192 -> 10.067, 128 -> 9.836, 64 -> 9.808, 32 -> 9.825. digest/outers identical in all five; h5diff every arm vs blk256 = 0; cmp CSV on the extremes (256 vs 32) CMP_IDENTICAL.
cmfd_block.occupancy: [CMFD][GRAPH] node_blocks/vector_blocks go 34/67 -> 45/89 -> 67/133 -> 133/265 -> 265/529 as block_threads go 256 -> 32. vector_blocks first clears 1x SM at 128 threads (133) and 2x SM at 64 (265). That 2x-SM bar is exactly what block 27's kernel census said was missing.
cmfd_block.why_not_32: 32 occupies more and is NOT faster (9.825 vs 9.808). More, smaller blocks eventually repay their better SM coverage in launch and grid-sync overhead; 64 is the knee on this deck.
cmfd_block.batch_exclusion: block 29d, 8xM8 + MPS 12 pct: 1176.1 c/h, -0.3 pct against the ~1180 reference. Flat. The batch bottleneck is not per-launch CMFD occupancy, so this knob stays out of the batch env.

cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.gate_class: B0 (h5diff 0 between auto and blocking on a single deck)
cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.default: auto. NOT part of this arm, in either mode.
cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.why_recorded_here: because it resolves an open question this campaign carried for two blocks, and because it is a real batch option someone will want. Batch 8xM8+MPS12: auto 1176.5 c/h at 72.8 pct CPU, blocking 1134.3 c/h (-3.6 pct) at 40.1 pct CPU, yield 1173.9 at 67.0 pct. All three [CUDA][SCHED] receipts confirm applied == requested with rc cudaSuccess, so the flag is not a no-op in any mode.
cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.what_it_settles: block 26 concluded that ~74 pct of batch CPU was real host work, on the strength of OMP_WAIT_POLICY=PASSIVE not changing it. That reading was WRONG: PASSIVE removes only OpenMP's own barrier spin, while cudaStreamSynchronize spins under cudaDeviceScheduleSpin, which is a separate device-schedule flag. Blocking drops CPU to 40.1 pct, so roughly 33 percentage points of that 74 was CUDA spin. perf and ncu are not installed on 238, so no intermediate settling measurement was possible.
cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.single_deck_is_the_mirror_image: auto 11.316 s vs blocking 12.296 s (+8.7 pct). A lone process has nothing to hand the freed cores to, so trading spin latency for a kernel-level wait/wake round trip is a straight loss.
cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.why_not_adopted: the bar was 'no c/h loss' and -3.6 pct does not clear it. Its value is what the freed CPU enables: 16xM8 goes 1035.3 -> 1159.5 c/h (+12.0 pct) under blocking, and 12xM8 +3.4 pct - which confirms CPU contention, not only MPS thread-share dilution, was part of why more concurrency lost. 8xM16 does not improve (-1.3 pct): its bottleneck is tail, not CPU.

rolling_refill_NOT_IN_ARM.why_recorded_here: because the mechanism works and the code is kept as scheduler substrate, and because its negative result is the most load-bearing finding of the session.
rolling_refill_NOT_IN_ARM.evidence_238: block 30 at bd7a0d3, 128-job manifest: 8xM8 auto 1186.1 -> rolling 1158.3 c/h (-2.3 pct); 8xM16 auto 1246.2 -> rolling 1181.2 (-5.2 pct); 8xM16 rolling+blocking 1109.8 (-6.1 pct vs rolling alone). The expected band was 1500-1900 c/h.

rolling_refill_NOT_IN_ARM.exactness: all 64 distinct candidate cases produced BIT-IDENTICAL per-case light-result digests between the auto and rolling claim modes, matched by case_key across all 8 workers - far exceeding the required >=8-case check.
rolling_refill_NOT_IN_ARM.receipt_gap: stale_tenant_refusals was not printed by this schema version. Not recorded as 0. The harness-level "stale_tenants":0 in the [MULTI_GPU][TOTAL] receipt is the closest confirmed zero-refusal signal available.
rolling_refill_NOT_IN_ARM.what_it_proves: arena fill was never the constraint. The mechanism drives slot idle to ~1 ms and the wave tail to 0 and throughput still falls, so the remaining cost is GPU time per case, not how the job list is sliced. Block 31 measures that directly.

throughput_baselines.deck_weight: MEASURED, not assumed, from block 30's own per-case receipts (255 samples across all 8 workers of the 8xM8-auto arm): the m64_manual decks average 51.0 statepoints and 8415.5 outers per case, against KNGR's 35 and 4377. That is 1.46x by statepoint and 1.92x by outer. m64 batch cases-per-hour must NOT be divided into a KNGR single-deck wall.
throughput_baselines.kngr_x64_arm: the SAME deck as the single-deck benchmark, 64 times: 8xM8 + MPS auto, bd7a0d3, v6 env. wall_s 114.274, 1.786 s/case, all 128 receipt lines read outers:4377, nvidia-smi dmon sm pct mean 94.8 / p95 100 / 94.7 pct of samples >= 85.
throughput_baselines.batch_mode_overhead: 1.786 s/case against the ~1.2 s/case single-deck GPU-kernel-time reference = 1.49x, i.e. batch mode itself costs about +49 pct more time per case, measured on the IDENTICAL deck so it cannot be deck weight. Inverted: batch runs at 67 pct of the single-deck kernel-time ideal. The m64 gap (~2.55x) is close to deck weight 1.92x times batch overhead 1.49x = 2.86x - both factors are real, and neither of the two clean either/or branches proposed beforehand matched the measurement.
throughput_baselines.where_the_49_percent_comes_from: PACKING WIDTH, NOT MPS. Block 32, all on the KNGR-x64 manifest: 1xM64 raw (no MPS) 1537.6 c/h vs 1xM8 raw (no MPS) 799.6 = width alone is 1.92x. 8xM8 with no MPS 1019.1 c/h vs 8xM8 with MPS 2016.2 = MPS is 1.98x FASTER, so MPS is the source of concurrency, not a source of overhead; removing it would make the per-case overhead worse, not better. Full sweep: 8xM8+MPS 2016.2 > 4xM16+MPS25 2001.2 > 2xM32+MPS50 1796.9 > 1xM64 raw 1537.6 > 8xM8 no-MPS 1019.1 > 1xM8 raw 799.6. All 5 arms 64/64 ok, 0 failed, 0 duplicates, 0 stale tenants, 0 isolation mismatches across 320 cases.
throughput_baselines.shape_sweep_128job: 8xM16 auto 1246.2 (bd7a0d3) / 1235.1 (cd3630c); 8xM8 auto 1186.1 / 1182.0; 8xM16 rolling 1181.2; 16xM8 blocking 1159.5; 8xM8 rolling 1158.3; 8xM16 rolling+blocking 1109.8; 16xM8 auto 1035.3; 16xM16 auto 1023.9; 8xM8 claim=4 978.0; 12xM8 blocking 976.3; 12xM8 auto 944.5; 8xM8 claim=2 840.3; 8xM8 claim=1 592.8.
throughput_baselines.shape_verdict: nothing beyond 8 processes helps at any width tried, and no --claim chunk size helps at all. 8xM8 and 8xM16 with claim=auto are the shapes to use.
throughput_baselines.block_25_confound_and_its_correction: the first concurrency sweep fed 12xM8 (96 slots) and 16xM8 (128 slots) from a 64-job pool, so width_fill could not arithmetically exceed 0.667 / 0.5. Redone on 128 jobs, width_fill RISES with more processes (0.4473 -> 0.4714 -> 0.5220) and throughput STILL falls - which is the first direct evidence that arena fill was never the constraint.
throughput_baselines.host_cpu: batch 8xM8+MPS12: auto 72.8 pct total CPU, blocking 40.1 pct, yield 67.0 pct. Roughly 33 percentage points of the long-reported ~74 pct is cudaStreamSynchronize spin, not host work. See arm_components.cuda_sync_mode_NOT_IN_ARM.

The batch worker's nsys invocation omitted --cuda-graph-trace=node (only the single-deck run in block 27a had it), so the CMFD/BiCG family (colored_block_sweep, matvec_two_group, the reduce_* family, prepare_p_jacobi, update_*_jacobi) returns ZERO rows in the batch trace - that trace holds only 19 distinct kernel names.
